validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE - confirmed, not GEM-only. The wiki page's sole citation ('Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' -> opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf) looked like it could be the generic-aggregate existence trap: the live URL now 200s but only serves the OPEC.org homepage shell (url_verifier FAILs for 'Attahaddy', as expected from a rotted link, not a content problem). I pulled the identical document from the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org/web/20250110032615/.../ASB2012.pdf), confirmed via `file` it is a genuine 7.8MB PDF (not an HTML stub), and ran `pdftotext -layout` on it directly. Page 75, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', under the 'Libya (cont'd)' header, contains the exact row: 'Attahaddy/km-91.5   Sirte Oil   25 [mi]   30 [in]   28,320,589 [1,000 scm/yr]'. Converting: 25 mi x 1.60934 = 40.23 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown=40.00 km almost exactly (0.6% off, pure rounding); capacity 28,320,589 thousand scm/yr = 28.320589 bcm/yr, matching GEM's Capacity=28.32 bcm/y to two decimals. This is the SAME document/table that seeded the whole 30-pipeline Libya-gas roster (confirmed by sibling shards P1868/P1869/P1871 finding matching rows for Km-81.5-Brega, Raguba-Km-110, and Sahel-km-81.5 respectively in the identical table; the table also carries the immediately adjacent 'Km-91.5/Brega' row for P1872), so this is a genuine, specific, non-GEM-derived citation naming this exact pipeline by name and page - the opposite of a generic aggregate mention. url_verifier's automated FAIL is a false negative documented in the tool's own docstring (binary-PDF byte stream, no text extraction) and independently reproduced by three sibling researchers on this same source. SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE: the Wikipedia 'Sirte Oil Company' article (url_verifier OK, 200, contains 'Attahaddy') lists Attahaddy among SOC's Non-Associated Gas Fields (alongside Hateiba, Sahl/Sahel, Assamoud, Meghil, Sorrah) and states 'As of 2005, besides Nasser, SOC was in charge of two other gas fields - Attahadi and Assumud - plus the Marsa el-Brega liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant,' with those fields feeding a Brega LNG plant processing ~900 million cubic meters/year as of 2005. This independently confirms Attahaddy is a real, currently-producing, non-associated gas field (not a hallucinated waypoint) operated by Sirte Oil Company and physically oriented toward Brega - consistent with a gas transmission line running from the Attahaddy field toward the km-91.5 junction that then continues to Brega via P1872. Neither this Wikipedia source nor any other found gives the exact length/diameter/capacity figures, so the numeric spec still rests on one strong source (OPEC); tier=medium overall, matching the convention used by sibling shards in this batch for the same table. CLASSIFICATION - correct as recorded: Fuel=Gas is right (Attahaddy is explicitly a non-associated gas field per Wikipedia, and OPEC's table is titled 'Gas pipelines'), and at 28.32 bcm/y this sits among Libya's other named trunk gas pipelines in the same OPEC table (Nasser/Brega 14.87, Km-91.5/Brega 21.24, Intesar/Brega 42.48), not a gathering/process line - no reclassification needed. DUPLICATE - checked against all 30 roster rows: not a duplicate. Capacity 28.32 bcm/y and the compound '30, 12 in' diameter are unique to this row; the OPEC table lists 'Attahaddy/km-91.5' and 'Km-91.5/Brega' (P1872) as two separate, sequential line items sharing the km-91.5 junction (an Attahaddy field -> km-91.5 -> Brega chain, the same segmenting convention already confirmed for the Intesar/Sahel/km-81.5/Brega chain in sibling shards P1869/P1871/P1868) - GEM correctly split these into two rows rather than double-counting one pipe. ATTRIBUTION - minor caveat only, not scored as wrong: GEM records Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' (100%); the OPEC source names operator 'Sirte Oil' for this row, and a 2013 Canadian IRB research response (hosted on ecoi.net, url_verifier OK, contains 'Sirte') independently confirms Sirte Oil Company is state-owned / a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Oil Corporation - so NOC as ultimate owner is defensible, though Sirte Oil Company would be the more precise operator entry (same pattern flagged by sibling shards for the other km-marker lines in this table). SPEC - length and capacity confirmed with no material disagreement (see existence section). One caveat, not escalated to a separate concern: GEM's Diameter='30, 12' (in) is a compound two-value field, but OPEC's table gives only a single diameter, 30 in, for this row - the '30' component matches exactly, but no source found corroborates the additional '12 in' value, so I have NOT added a ref to the Diameter field as fully confirmed (see fills: marked UNRESOLVED rather than force-citing a source that only supports half the value). This is a gap in corroboration, not a contradiction, so I'm not opening a separate concern object for it.
